Title: dumb Q - but I want to be sure

Messages.Author: jeroen rombouts
Messages.Body:
Greetz,

I have a (IMO stupid) question, but it has caused a debate the last time we
played.

1) Can you play Backstab on a strike that already has First Strike (eg sup
Fast hands)? And what will be the effect of this?

The situation was s/t like this:
Meth A rushes B's minion with a Muddled with a Sengir Dagger. B's Minion
blocks and plays Backstab and Fast Hands. Does B's minion get the Sengir
before he is hit for 4agg damage? In short does 'First first Strike' exist.
I'm guessing not, but just to make sure.

2) redrawing

Wynn, with 7 Raptors, rushes another players vamp, with a Bum's rush.
This -the rushed one- vamp blocks, to get rid of the manuever. Wynn Form of
Mists and continues to Rush.

Does the controller of the rushed vamp have to redraw (and rediscard!)
between the playing of the Fom and the start of the rush. I'm guessing he
has, but the others I was playing with say that Wynn never left combat and
that they didn' have to redraw and discard. Because I was biased - it was my
Wynn - nobody really listened to my arguments.

Jeroen

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
"jeroen rombouts" <jeroen....@pandora.be> wrote:
> 1) Can you play Backstab on a strike that already has First Strike (eg
> sup Fast hands)? And what will be the effect of this?

You can play Backstab and then use a strike that already has FIrst
Strike, yes. The effect will be that the strike is done at First
Strike (as it would have been anyhow - the Backstab has no effect
in this case).

> 2) redrawing
>
> Wynn, with 7 Raptors, rushes another players vamp, with a Bum's rush.
> This -the rushed one- vamp blocks, to get rid of the manuever. Wynn
> Form of Mists and continues to Rush.
>
> Does the controller of the rushed vamp have to redraw (and rediscard!)
> between the playing of the Fom and the start of the rush. I'm guessing
> he has, but the others I was playing with say that Wynn never left
> combat and that they didn' have to redraw and discard. Because I was
> biased - it was my Wynn - nobody really listened to my arguments.

He clearly left combat - there was a period of "do you block" in between
the first (block-induced) combat and the second (successful-action)
combat. In that period, the "victim" draws up to her hand size, whic
is not reduced by Raptors.

Let me see if I understand what you said...

Minion A (with 7 superior Raptors) rushes Minion B. Minion B blocks.
Minion B's controllers hand size drops by 7 cards. Minion A's
controller plays Form of Mist at superior. Minion B's controller draws
up to a full hand because the block induced combat is over. The action
continues at +1 stealth and another combat starts.

I made it this far, but why do you say that Minion B's controller would
not have a reduced hand size for the successful action combat?
